about: Public fixture rows for the LiteRT conversion of decider-2b-vision. Every image is a synthetic drawing made with PIL for this check (colour cards, shapes, text, and simple Pong- and Breakout-style game frames); none is a photograph, a screenshot or an emulator render. Values are the upstream model in float32 on CPU, read with the checkpoint's own decider/vision.py prepare() + slot_logits(), unmodified, softmax at T = 1.

oracle.batch: one request per forward, no padding

arms.g256_mrope: the author's code on image_256 (the original resized to 256 x 256 with PIL BICUBIC); the LiteRT files are checked against this arm
arms.author: the author's code on the original image (its own dynamic resolution); the difference from g256_mrope is the cost of the fixed 256 x 256 input
arms.g256_pos1d: as g256_mrope, but with the rotary positions replaced by plain 1-D positions 0, 1, 2, ... on all three channels (what a 1-D position contract gives); the difference from g256_mrope is why the LiteRT decoder derives the 3-channel positions in its graph
